title: 20.9 An Autonomous and Lightweight Microactuator Driving System Using Flying Solid-State Batteries
problem: Small-scale flying electromechanical systems (microrobotics) require efficient high-voltage drive systems for electrostatic and piezoelectric actuators while meeting stringent weight (<1-2g) and power constraints for flight endurance (10s of minutes).
motivation: Capacitive actuators demand reactive power (Cx V² F) in the 10s mW range; efficient energy management is critical for flight autonomy limited by micro-scale energy storage capacity.
method: The system uses solid-state batteries (compact, integrated energy sources with no liquid electrolyte) built into the microrobot to convert its low-voltage battery power (3-5V) into high voltages (tens of volts) for the electrostatic and piezoelectric actuators. The design optimizes how efficiently this conversion happens and manages energy delivery to the capacitive loads (electrical charges that power the actuators).
key_novelty: Solid-state batteries integrated into flying microrobots enable lightweight, efficient power conversion from low to high voltage for driving microactuators.
contributions: Lightweight autonomous microactuator driving system for flying systems
Solid-state battery integration for high-voltage generation from low-voltage sources
Efficient reactive power management for capacitive actuators
primary_theme: Lightweight microactuator drive for flying robots
